title: Prism flip label: a quarter turn that rolls a copy of the label into view
intent: Nav and link labels that turn like a block
summary: Each `[data-prism]` link ships as its plain label; the module wraps it in a `transform-style: preserve-3d` box holding the label on a front face (`translateZ(d)`) and an `aria-hidden` copy on the face below (`rotateX(-90deg) translateZ(d)`), with `backface-visibility: hidden` and `d` measured as half the box's own height, and sets the box back by `translateZ(-d)` so the front face rests exactly in the page plane and the box turns about its own centre; hover (fine pointers only, `(hover: hover)`) and `:focus-visible` turn it `rotateX(90deg)` under `perspective: 1000px` on its parent over `400 ms` expo-out, after which the copy sits on the label's exact box; four header cells roll to an inked cell while their siblings dim to `.55`, footer links roll to an inverted tile, and the `letters` variant builds one prism per letter inside no-wrap words with a `24 ms` stagger and a visually hidden label as the accessible name; touch gets no turn but a filled press state; reduced motion and static swap the two faces in place by opacity (`120 ms`, none in static) with no transform; forced colours show the plain label
variants: whole label, header cells and footer links (this, default)
one prism per letter with a 24 ms stagger (`data-prism="letters"`, the film list here)
perspective applied only while a box is turning, as the source does, for text that must stay on the page's own raster at rest
a third face: turn 180° about X to show a face on the back, for a label that says something different (a count, a date) rather than repeating itself
